title: Windowed ingest and non‑blocking republish protocol
creator: Aisha Mensah
description:
Current queue consumers occasionally create head-of-line blocking when slow reenqueue or lease reconciliation paths perform synchronous Redis/Kafka operations. This ticket refactors the ingest and republish flow to a windowed, non-blocking pattern: 1) introduce an ingest window per shard to bound inflight work and reduce global contention; 2) make republish (dead-letter/requeue) asynchronous with cooperative backpressure; 3) move lease reconciliation off the hot path into a best-effort reconciler; 4) upgrade Redis client to async-native to remove blocking IO; 5) expose metrics and a rollout plan.

Goals:
- Eliminate head-of-line blocking caused by synchronous requeue paths
- Reduce tail latency variance under bursty traffic
- Improve throughput on 99th percentile SLOs by 15-30%
- Provide safe rollback and incremental rollout for Dedicated tenants

Non-goals:
- Full redesign of partitioning/sharding strategy (out of scope)

Technical approach:
- Add 'ingest-window' token allocator per shard (configurable window size, default 128) to limit inflight requests and provide fairness between tenants.
- Convert republish/requeue to an idempotent, async pipeline: enqueue requeue requests to a local in-memory channel that drains at a controlled concurrency to Redis/Kafka; implement exponential jittered backoff and cap retry credits per tenant.
- Move lease reconciliation to a background reconciler that runs periodically with cooperative cancellation; reconcile only when drift > threshold.
- Swap blocking Redis client with async-native client (see dependency upgrade section) and update connection pooling to prefer non-blocking event-loop threads.
- Add graceful shutdown hooks that drain the ingest window with a bounded timeout before terminating.

Metrics and alerts:
- new metrics: ingest_window_inflight, republish_queue_len, republish_failures, lease_reconcile_rate, lease_reconcile_latency
- dashboard: runtime/ingest/windowing (links in comments)
- alert: republish_failures > 0.5% for 5m or republish_queue_len > 3x baseline

Migration and rollout:
1) Feature-flag the new windowed allocator per shard
2) Canary in a single low-traffic region + synthetic load test
3) Ramp to 10% shards, monitor metrics and SLOs
4) Full rollout with fallback to legacy path if key metrics regress

Testing:
- unit tests for allocator invariants and idempotent requeue
- integration tests against kafka/redis test clusters
- chaos tests: simulate redis latency, consumer restarts, network partitions
- load tests: compare 99p latency and throughput vs baseline

Docs & artifacts:
- Confluence design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Windowed+Ingest+and+Republish+Design
- Load test dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/ingest-window/load-tests
- PRs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4102

Roll-forward criteria:
- no regression in 99p latency after 72h of canary at 10% capacity
- republish_failures < 0.2% and republish_queue_len stable
- unit/integration/chaos tests green

Rollback criteria:
- sustained increase in 99p latency > 20% or error budget burn > 30% in 1h

Trade-offs considered:
- Synchronous republish is simpler and reduces duplication; async republish increases complexity but decouples producer latency and improves tail behavior.
- Lease reconciliation moved off hot path may temporarily allow slightly stale leases, but we enforce thresholds and faster reconcile on detection of contention.
- Upgrading Redis client requires careful vetting; see dependencies.
